Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 56, verse 41–48:

{41 – 44} The intended meaning of "the companions of the left" (ashab al-shimal) is the people of the Fire and of ominous deeds. {45 – 48} Then He mentions their deeds that brought them to this recompense, saying: {Indeed, they had been before that affluent (mutrafin)}; that is, their worldly life had distracted them, they worked for it, and they enjoyed and indulged in it. Hope diverted them from doing good deeds; this affluence is what Allah censured them for. {And they used to persist in the great violation (al-hinth al-'azim)}; that is, they used to commit major sins, did not repent from them, did not feel remorse for them, but persisted in what angers their Lord, so they came before Him burdened with many sins that were not forgiven. They also used to deny the resurrection, saying, considering it far-fetched: {When we die and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected? And our forefathers of old?}; that is, how could we be raised after our death, when we have decayed and become dust and bones! This is impossible.

This is the food with which they try to repel hunger, and it is that which neither nourishes nor satisfies from hunger.

{54 – 56} As for their drink: it is the worst of drinks, and it is that they drink upon this food from boiling water (al-hamim) that seethes in their bellies. {Drinking like the drinking of the thirsty camels (al-hiim)}: and these are camels that are severely thirsty, or that al-Hiyam is a disease that afflicts camels, such that they are never satisfied from drinking water. {This}: the food and drink {is their welcome (nuzul)}; that is, their hospitality {on the Day of Recompense (al-Din)}: and it is the hospitality which they sent ahead for themselves and preferred over the hospitality of Allah for His friends. Allah the Exalted said: {Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a welcome, abiding therein forever, they will not desire any removal from them.}

Is not the One Who is capable of that capable of giving life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is over all things competent. For this reason He rebuked them for their not believing in the resurrection while they witness what is greater than it and more evident.

This is a blessing from Him upon His servants, by which He calls them to His tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), to worship Him, and to turn to Him in repentance. He has bestowed upon them what He facilitated for them of tilling for crops and fruits, so that there comes forth from that food, provisions, and fruits that are among their necessities, needs, and interests, which they cannot count, let alone thank Him for them or render their due. So He made them acknowledge His favor, and said:

﴿Do you cultivate it, or are We the Cultivators?﴾; that is: Did you bring it forth as a plant from the earth? Or did you make it grow? Or did you bring forth its ears and its fruit until it became grain ready for harvest and ripe fruit? Or is it God alone who has exclusive power over this and bestowed it upon you, while the most you can do is plough the earth, break it up, and cast the seed into it, and then you have no knowledge of what will happen after that and no power to do more than that?

Along with this, He alerted them that this tillage is exposed to dangers were it not for God's protection and His preservation of it as a provision and enjoyment for you for a time. So He said:

﴿If We willed, We would make it into debris﴾; that is: the sown crop and what is in it of fruits would become crushed fragments with no benefit in them and no provision. ﴿Then you would be left﴾; that is: you would become, because of its being made into debris after you had toiled over it and spent great sums, ﴿lamenting﴾; that is: you would regret and grieve over what had befallen you, and your joy, delight, and enjoyment would vanish thereby. So you would say: ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt﴾; that is: we have suffered loss, and a calamity has struck us that has wiped us out. Then, after that, you would recognize from where you were brought low and by what cause you were struck. So you would say: ﴿Rather, we are deprived!﴾ Therefore, praise God, the Exalted, for having caused it to grow for you, then preserved it and perfected it for you, and did not send upon it the blights by which you would be deprived of its benefit and goodness.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 56, verse 75–87:

{75 – 76} God, exalted is He, swears by the stars and their setting places, meaning their falling at their settings, and by what God brings about at those times of events that point to His greatness, His majesty and His oneness. Then He magnifies this thing sworn by, saying: ﴿And indeed it is a mighty oath, if you only knew﴾. The oath is mighty because in the stars, their movement, and their setting, there are signs and lessons that cannot be counted.

{77} As for what is sworn to, it is the affirmation of the Qur'an, that it is the truth with no doubt in it and no uncertainty affecting it, and that it is ﴿noble﴾; that is, abundant in good and rich in knowledge. Every good and every knowledge is derived from the Book of God and deduced from it.

{78} ﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾; that is, hidden from the eyes of creation. This well-guarded Book is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz); that is, this Qur'an is written in the Preserved Tablet, honored with God and with His angels in the Highest Assembly.
It is also possible that the intended "well-guarded Book" is the book that is in the hands of the angels whom God sends down with His revelation and message, and that the meaning is that it is hidden from the devils, who have no power to alter it, to add to or subtract from it, or to steal it.

{79} ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾; that is, none touches the Qur'an except the noble angels, whom God has purified from calamities, sins and defects. Since none touches it except the purified, and since the people of impurity and the devils have no capacity or power to touch it, the verse indicates, as a warning, that it is not permissible for anyone to touch the Qur'an except one who is in a state of purity [as the hadith has reported, and for this reason it has been said that the verse is a report with the meaning of a prohibition; that is, none should touch the Qur'an except one who is pure].

{80} ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾; that is, this Qur'an, described with those sublime attributes, is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds, who nurtures His servants with His religious and worldly blessings. The most sublime nurturing with which He has nurtured His servants is His sending down this Qur'an, which includes the benefits of both abodes, and through which God has shown mercy to the servants with a mercy for which they cannot give thanks. Among what is obligatory upon them is that they stand by it, proclaim it, call to it, and speak it out openly.

{81} For this reason He said: ﴿Then is it this discourse that you disdain?﴾; that is, is it this mighty Book and wise Reminder that you disdain? ﴿Do you disdain it?﴾; that is, do you conceal and deceive out of fear of people, their shame and their tongues? This is not fitting and not appropriate! Rather, what is fitting is to be lenient toward speech whose speaker is not confident of it. As for the Noble Qur'an, it is the truth, by which no contender contends without being overcome, and no assailant assails with it without being above the other, and it is the one that is not to be disdained or concealed, but rather to be proclaimed and made public.

{82} His saying: ﴿And you make your provision that you deny﴾; that is, you make the repayment of God's favor upon you in provision to be denial and disbelief in God's blessing, so you say: "We were given rain by such-and-such a star!" and you attribute the blessing to other than the one who bestows and grants it. Why do you not thank God for His kindness in sending it down to you so that He may increase you from His bounty? For denial and disbelief call for the removal of blessings and the descent of punishments.

{83 – 85} ﴿Then why, when it reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on — and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see﴾; that is, why not, when the soul reaches the throat, and you are looking at the dying person in this state, while We are nearer to him than you by Our knowledge and Our angels, but you do not perceive.

{86 – 87} ﴿Then why, if you are not to be held accountable﴾; that is, why not, since you claim that you will not be resurrected, nor called to account, nor recompensed, to return the soul to its body ﴿if you are truthful﴾, while you acknowledge that you are powerless to return it to its place? Then either you acknowledge the truth brought by Muhammad (ﷺ), or you obstinately deny it and your state and the evil of your final outcome will be known.
